brief: A planter for a sunny kitchen windowsill with three herbs growing in it.

requirements.evidence: 3 full cells in a row (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:2,0,0;full) each with a drained full-depth bin (bin:0,0,0 / 1,0,0 / 2,0,0); check_build ok, meshClash clear; look sees all 3 plants.
Compact single-row 1x3 layout suits a narrow sill; plants visible in look view. Heat/UV resistance depends on the user's chosen print material, which the configurator does not check.
requirements.requirement: Suited to a sunny windowsill (small footprint, sun exposure)

requirements.evidence: fill_and_plant placed basil-young (prop:1), parsley-young (prop:2), chives-young (prop:3), each in soil in its own bin; no prop warnings.

finish.summary: Linear 3-cell drained-bin planter with basil, parsley and chives growing in soil. House rules applied, checks clear, all three plants visible.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
